answer: Each identity must lock a bond before it can act, so creating clones means capital at risk rather than a free mask. To forge a hundred sybils, an attacker must post a hundred deposits. When detection links clones through shared behavior, slashing seizes the entire bond, pushing the attacker toward the nadir of their budget instead of profit. A lone honest agent stakes a small marble, but a swarm must stake it many times over, making fakery costly and self-defeating.
